issues.issue: Trial name labels Study 11 as 'placebo-controlled monotherapy trial' but the only citation merely lists it among three monotherapy studies; the monotherapy/placebo-controlled descriptors are not supported by this quote.

Design states '24-week' for Study CV181011 but the citation describing the 24-week duration refers to 'two 24-week trials' collectively and the 401-patient quote ('first trial') is not tied to Study 11; it conflates two different studies' details into one trial.
N=401 is drawn from 'the first trial' quote, which is not identified as Study CV181011; the citation does not confirm 401 belongs to Study 11.
The result (Table 3, 401-patient 'first trial') is attributed to Study CV181011 but no citation links that monotherapy efficacy table to Study 11 specifically.

The review states three Phase 2/3 monotherapy studies (CV181008, CV181011, CV18138) were designed, yet only one pivotal trial is recorded, an internal inconsistency in trial count vs. trials described.

Peripheral edema is stated as 'ONGLYZA 5 mg plus TZD (8.1% vs 4.3% placebo)' but the citation says add-on to TZD trial; combining add-on TZD, add-on glyburide hypoglycemia, and monotherapy AE rates mixes different trial populations into one 'key safety' narrative without distinguishing them clearly.

The headline AEs (URTI 7.7%, UTI 6.8%, headache 6.5%) describe a specific pooled/monotherapy table, but are presented as the generic 'most common adverse reactions'; the characterization slightly overstates what the single table citation supports.
Automated flags for numbers '30' and '2008' in the detail are false positives (they are part of the receipt date June 30, 2008, which is excluded as a date); no action needed.
Automated flag for the number '5' is a false positive — it refers to the ONGLYZA 5 mg dose, which is dose-excluded and is supported by the design/N citations.
